newsitem.title: USA: MMI faces $5.1 mln judgment from UK court.
newsitem.headline: MMI faces $5.1 mln judgment from UK court.

text.p: MMI Cos Inc said Thursday that a court in the United Kingdom on February 12 rendered, then largely stayed pending appeal, a $5.1 million judgment plus costs and expenses against it.

The judgment, which includes $1.3 million in interest, involves the 1992 sale by MMI of Ludgate Insurance Cos Ltd to London-based Ken Randall Associated Ltd, and a subsequent dispute over sales contract warranties.
MMI said it treated the sale as a discontinued operation on its 1992 consolidated financial statements.

MMI said it sold Ludgate for $3.8 million, including $350,000 in cash and a contingent note for $3,450,000 payable in three equal annual installments, which were subject to adjustment for changes to Ludgate's insurance reserves.
Two installment dates have passed without any payments, MMI said.

MMI maintained that, under sales contract terms, damages in any warranty dispute were capped at the amount of consideration. One issue in an appeal, the company added, would be whether the damages cap is $350,000 or $3.8 million.

MMI said it was ordered by the U.K. court to pay Randall within a week $470,000, based on Randall's initial $350,000 payment plus interest. The judge stayed payment of the remainder pending appeal and ordered it placed in an escrow account within 28 days, MMI said.

"We intend to pursue a vigorous appeal in the Court of Appeal and have been advised by U.K. lawyers that our prospects of success are good for limiting the extent of MMI's liability to the actual amount of $350,000 paid by Randall plus cost and interest," B. Frederick Becker, chairman of MMI, said in a statement.

Becker said MMI may resume pursuit of a counterclaim in the U.K. against Randall, seeking payment of the two unpaid installments as well as the upcoming final installment of the Ludgate sales prices. That counterclaim would be based on MMI's assertions that Ludgate's performance after 1992 met targets that would trigger payments by Randall.

MMI said a lawsuit filed by Randall in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois is also pending. That suit relates to a reinsurance agreement involving American Continental Insurance Co, an MMI subsidiary.
MMI said it has filed a summary judgment seeking dismissal of the suit. A ruling is expected this spring, it added.
MMI is a health care risk management company, providing professional liability insurance and reinsurance, risk management and other services.
